title: Auto Loans: Installment Payments by Transfer from PCB Checking
content:
Borrowers of Piedmont Crescent Bank Auto Loans can ask the bank to pay an overdue installment for them by moving money out of their own PCB checking account. This page covers that service and the action through which it is booked.

## When this applies

The service answers a borrower's request that PCB pay the earliest installment of an auto loan that is past due, by transfer from a PCB checking account in the borrower's own name. The agent books one scheduled payment for the borrower, credited toward that installment; the installment in question is the one falling due on the loan's next payment due date. A payment booked this way stays with the installment it pays: it never runs on into the installment after it and never counts toward a later installment ahead of time.

## Business effect

The payment is recorded on the loan's activity as a scheduled payment made by PCB transfer and credited today, divided into a fees share, an interest share and a principal share. Where the fees share is above zero, a matching fee settlement is recorded as well. The loan's unpaid principal falls by the principal share and its unpaid fees fall by the fees share; today becomes the last payment date; and the next installment due date and the days past due supplied with the payment are recorded on the loan. The borrower can afterwards see the payment, its division and the new balances.

## Invoking the action

The action is `post_installment_payment_660c6229`, an agent-side tool that is hidden until needed: the agent unlocks it and then calls it directly on the borrower's behalf.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_loan_id` | reference number of the loan being paid, from the borrower's auto loan lookup | identifier |
| `installment_due_date` | due date of the installment this payment is credited toward; never left empty | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `amount` | total drawn from the checking account | positive USD, two decimals |
| `fees_portion` | part of the payment going to fees due | USD, two decimals; 0.00 when no fees are paid |
| `interest_portion` | part going to accrued interest | USD, two decimals |
| `principal_portion` | part going to principal | USD, two decimals |
| `counterparty_account_id` | reference number of the borrower's PCB checking account the money comes from, from the checking account lookup | identifier |
| `next_payment_due_date` | due date of the earliest installment that will still be unsatisfied once this payment has posted | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `days_past_due` | the loan's days past due once this payment has posted | whole calendar days, zero or more; 0 when nothing is past due |

## Receipt

A successful call returns status "posted" together with `payment_reference` (a 12-digit payment reference number), `auto_txn_id` (the new payment entry), `fee_settlement_id` (the fee settlement entry, or "" when the fees share is 0.00), `principal_balance` and `fees_due` (the unpaid principal and fees afterwards, two decimals), `next_payment_due_date` and `days_past_due`.
